data.narrative:
Teradar is a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by MIT-trained CEO Matt Carey, with CTO Gregory Charvat (ex-CTO of Humatics) and Chief Chip Architect Nick Saiz leading terahertz IC development. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable set of 10 firms across Defense & Security at the same stage: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Defense Unicorns, and Heven AeroTech.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression anchors to the $175M in total capital raised and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $332M. Peer-median valuation across 6 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $1.1B, with a peer range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The median valuation across this peer set is $1.1B, reflecting Dream Security at $3.0B as an upper outlier and smaller peers clustered near $1.0B.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $283M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $729M. Stage-progression anchors the lower bound, while peer-median data supports the upper bound. Key uncertainties include Teradar's revenue traction and capital efficiency relative to peer cohorts, differentiation of its terahertz IP relative to competitors, and defense-sector procurement cycle risk—all material to positioning within the $283M–$1.3B range.
